content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Managing Indexes in MongoDB"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Indexes are special data structures that store a small portion of the collection's data in an easy-to-traverse form. They store the value of a specific field or set of fields, ordered by the value of the field. Indexing allows MongoDB to efficiently resolve queries without scanning every document in a collection."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating Indexes"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create indexes using the `createIndex()` method. This method takes a document that specifies the fields to index and the index type (ascending or descending)."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"db.collection.createIndex( { item: 1, quantity: -1 } )"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the above example, an index is created on the 'item' field in ascending order (1) and the 'quantity' field in descending order (-1)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Index Types"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Single Field: Index on a single field. Example: `db.collection.createIndex( { item: 1 } )`"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Compound: Index on multiple fields. Example: `db.collection.createIndex( { item: 1, quantity: -1 } )`"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Multikey: Index on an array field. MongoDB automatically creates these when indexing a field that holds an array."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Text: Supports text search queries on string content. Example: `db.collection.createIndex( { description: \"text\" } )`"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Geospatial: Supports geospatial queries on location data."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Index Options"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Unique: Prevents inserting documents where the indexed field(s) match an existing value. Example: `db.collection.createIndex( { item: 1 }, { unique: true } )`"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"TTL (Time-To-Live): Automatically removes documents after a certain amount of time. Example: `db.collection.createIndex( { \"lastModifiedDate\": 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 3600 } )`"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Partial Filtered Indexes: Only indexes documents that match a specified filter expression. Example: `db.collection.createIndex( { rating: 1 }, { partialFilterExpression: { rating: { $gt: 5 } } } )`"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Listing Indexes"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can list all indexes on a collection using the `getIndexes()` method."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"db.collection.getIndexes()"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Dropping Indexes"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can drop indexes using the `dropIndex()` or `dropIndexes()` methods."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"db.collection.dropIndex( { item: 1, quantity: -1 } )"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"db.collection.dropIndexes()"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Index Performance"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use the `explain()` method to analyze query performance and determine if indexes are being used effectively. This method provides detailed information about the query execution plan."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"db.collection.find( { item: \"xyz\" } ).explain(\"executionStats\")"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"Proper index management is crucial for maintaining optimal MongoDB performance. Regularly review your indexes and drop any that are no longer needed."}]
